column3: Look up function number AX in the (fn#,offset) table of registered driver BX (0..15); returns far ptr into the driver image or NULL
Common stub target: dispatch API function AX to the driver whose handle is the first stack argument (tail-jumps into the driver; returns 0 if unsupported)

INT 08h handler: re-entrancy guard, own stack in CS, for each of 17 timer slots in state 2 add the PIT period (us) to its accumulator and call it when >= its period; EOI; integrity check of the CS 'Test' marker
Clear all timer states/accumulators/periods and set the current PIT period to 0xFFFFFFFF
Timer slot 16 callback: chain to the original INT 08h handler (BIOS clock) via PUSHF + far call
Save the INT 08h vector and install ail_timer_isr; slot 16 callback = ail_bios_tick_chain
Restore the saved INT 08h vector and stop servicing timers
Program PIT channel 0 in mode 3 with the given 16-bit divisor (0 = 65536) and remember it
Set PIT period in microseconds: divisor = us*10000/8380, or 0 (18.2 Hz) when us >= 54925
Unsigned 32/32 division helper (shift-subtract loop when the divisor exceeds 16 bits)
Find the smallest period among allocated timers; if it changed reprogram the PIT and clear all accumulators
Initialise AIL: clear the 16 driver slots, their timer handles (-1) and initialised flags
For every registered driver release its service timer and shut it down (passing the sign-off message), then release all timers
Allocate a timer slot (0..15) for a far callback; on the first timer reset the table, create the BIOS-chain slot 16 (54925 us) and hook INT 08h; returns handle or -1
Free a timer slot; when none remain restore the default PIT rate and unhook INT 08h
Release timer handles 15..0
Timer state 1 (allocated) -> 2 (running)
Start timers 15..0
Timer state 2 (running) -> 1 (stopped)
Stop timers 15..0
Set a timer period in microseconds (32-bit), reset its accumulator and recompute the PIT rate
Set a timer frequency in Hz (32-bit): period = 1000000/Hz
Set a timer by PIT divisor: period = divisor*10000/11932 us (0 -> 54925 us)
Return the PIT divisor currently programmed (callback handed to drivers)
Register a loaded driver image: must contain 'Copy' at +2 (function table at +[0]); describe it and check its minimum API version <= 0xD3; returns handle 0..15 or -1
Forget driver slot n
Driver function 100: return far ptr to the driver descriptor (type, data suffix, default IO/IRQ/DMA/DRQ, service rate)
Driver function 101 (driver, IO, IRQ, DMA, DRQ): non-zero if the hardware responds
If the driver has a service rate register a timer for its function 103 at that frequency, call function 102 (driver, IO, IRQ, DMA, DRQ), mark initialised and start the timer
If initialised: release the driver's service timer and call function 104 (sign-off message)
